Bulk actions are ready at **http://maker:4001** (refresh). Let's walk through them.

**Action 1 — select a few and act together.** Save several links. A checkbox now sits on each bookmark. Tick two or three. A blue bar appears showing "N selected" with actions. Click **Add tags…**, type something like `reading, 2026`, and confirm — the tag is added to all the selected ones at once. Try **Mark finished** on the selection too, and confirm they all move.

**Action 2 — act on an entire view/search.** Type a search (or switch to a tab) so the list shows a filtered set. Then tick **"Select all in this view"** at the top — it selects *only* the bookmarks currently shown (the results of your search/view), not anything outside that filter. Now apply a bulk action (say **Archive**) — it affects exactly that filtered set.

**Action 3 — bulk remove/delete.** With some selected, try **Remove tags…** (removes a tag from all of them), and **Delete** (asks for one confirmation, then removes them all). In the **Archived** tab, selecting items offers **Restore** and **Delete permanently** instead.

Things I decided that I'd like you to confirm:
- The way to "apply to everything in the current view" is the **"Select all in this view"** checkbox — it deliberately covers only what's currently filtered/searched, so you can see exactly what you're acting on. Does that match what you meant?
- The bulk actions offered are: **add tags, remove tags, mark To-read, mark finished, archive, delete** (and restore/delete in the Archive). Is that the right set?
- Tag entry for bulk add/remove is via a quick typed prompt. Good enough, or would you want something else?

Does this bulk behavior match what you need?
